This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **131** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b5e4686b0464fcbc19873c24b9a477fd5a0bfa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `14df4a930637ed491ea85fefc78c1d5c4d4465b9` — the merge of head `336a2469d971313bfb0ed51f69c08f324213d43e` into base `f2b5e4686b0464fcbc19873c24b9a477fd5a0bfa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 14df4a930637ed491ea85fefc78c1d5c4d4465b9 && git checkout 14df4a930637ed491ea85fefc78c1d5c4d4465b9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2b5e4686b0464fcbc19873c24b9a477fd5a0bfa 336a2469d971313bfb0ed51f69c08f324213d43e && git checkout -B drift-repro f2b5e4686b0464fcbc19873c24b9a477fd5a0bfa && git merge --no-ff 336a2469d971313bfb0ed51f69c08f324213d43e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b5e4686b0464fcbc19873c24b9a477fd5a0bfa
```

## ACCEPT with a ruling — the dev caught a conflict between triage's acceptance criteria and this seat's own dispatch fence, and resolved it the right way

`domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`, at **2026-09-08T15:31Z**, head `336a2469d`. **Tier fuse:** **145** harness-stamped `"model"` values, all `claude-opus-5`, zero others — at the dispatched tier. ⛔ No self-description accepted.

### ⭐ Triage's loose end: the quotation was accurate all along, and the miss was an instrument artifact

Triage could not find the card's quoted *"indistinguishable by construction … are the same bytes"* on `stripProvisionedPrimaryFrom` and asked the next dev to locate the **symbol**. The dev did, and reported the quotation **matches this repo**. Re-derived by this seat on `origin/main`:

- `registry.ts:2754-2757` reads *"…the two are **indistinguishable by construction** — the read serves one body, and \"the author wrote `nameField: 'name'`\" and \"the read derived `nameField: 'name'`\" are the **same bytes**…"*
- `grep -c 'indistinguishable by construction'` → **0**, which **reproduces triage's miss exactly**.
- The multiline form hits: `indistinguishable by` / `* construction` — **split across a line wrap with a `*` continuation**.

⇒ ⭐ Not wording drift and not a cloud-tree quotation: **a single-line grep against a wrapped comment**. The card was right, triage's instrument was.

⚠️ And this seat repeated the same class one step later: my own `grep 'function stripProvisionedPrimaryFrom'` returned nothing, because it is a **class method** — `private stripProvisionedPrimaryFrom<T>(base: T): T` at **`:2764`**, exactly where the dev said. Three greps in a row today whose zero was the pattern's fault, not the tree's.

### Ruling on the flagged conflict: **option A — the dev's reading stands.** ⛔ My fence was the over-broad half.

**Triage criterion 2** required the `derived` half to ship in the same paragraph (*"do not fix only the explicit line"*). **My dispatch fenced it**: *"⛔ Do not act on the `derived`-is-dead-code observation … it was measured **in cloud**, not here."*

Read literally, my fence would have left a triage acceptance criterion unmet. The dev did not silently pick a side — it took the **intersection** and flagged it: a provenance-framed reachability sentence about `derived`, **measured on this tree** via the read-exit chain (including the `declinedBaseLayerStamps` withhold exception), with cloud's call-site dead-code finding **excluded** and cloud tool names absent from the diff.

⭐ Its argument is correct and is the reason I am ruling A: *"the fence's stated ground is a mechanism claim ('it was measured in cloud, not here'), and that mechanism **IS** measurable here."* My concern was **unmeasured provenance**, and I wrote it as a ban on the **conclusion**. The dev measured it here, so the fence is satisfied in substance while my wording said otherwise. ⇒ the fence was mine to write more precisely, ⛔ not the dev's to obey past its own reason.

### Verified, ⛔ not accepted on the report

- **Nothing published moves in shape.** `check:generated` → exit 0, *"All 15 generated artifacts are up to date"* ⇒ this docblock feeds **neither** `content/docs/references/` **nor** `api-surface/`. The `patch` changeset is nonetheless right and measured: the text lands in `dist/data/index.d.ts` + `.d.mts`, which `packages/spec` ships in `files[]`.
- ⭐ **The ablation is the right one, and the dev said why the obvious one would have been worthless.** These are **behavioural** pins, so "restore the old sentence" would **not** redden them. It mutated the mechanism instead — `provisionPrimary`'s designation `return { ...objectMeta, nameField: resolved }` → `return objectMeta` — and got **10 failed / 36 passed** with **both new pins failing by name**. Landing proven on disk (anchor 1→0, injected anchor 1, blob `ba635e0e` → `a416adb9`), restoration proven by **state** (empty `git diff HEAD`, empty porcelain, blob back to `ba635e0e`, 0 markers), under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`.
- **Scope holds:** 36 comment lines, **0 deletions** in the source; no predicate, no grade computation, no accept set moved — which is what the card demanded, since it states the predicate is *correct*.

### Recorded from the report, ⛔ neither filed nor re-derived

The repo's **only** grade consumer, `packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.ts:95`, reads **only** `status === 'none'` — so it was never exposed to the `explicit` misreading, and its input is the authored config (the pre-write side). ⇒ the three wrong artifacts this card counts were all **cloud-side** readers, which sharpens rather than weakens the card: the misreading travelled to the consumer that had no local pin to catch it.
